title: A smooth generic component in a nodal neighbourhood has a flat closure and finite etale boundary
statement:
Let $R\subset L$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$ [def-weil-field], so for every $a\in L^\times$ either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ belongs to $R$. Assume $L$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] and the primes of $R$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\xi$. Let $p:Z\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with geometrically reduced fibres (every field extension of each residue field gives a reduced fibre [def-pc-reduced-scheme]). Let $A$ be an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Z_\xi$, with reduced induced structure, and suppose $A$ is smooth and geometrically integral over $L$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $H\subset Z$ be its reduced closed closure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Suppose there is an open neighbourhood $N\subset Z$ containing all of $H$ such that $N\to S$ is nodal: every singular point of each geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $Q\hookrightarrow N$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], etale over $S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], contained in the relative smooth locus. Then $H$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $H\to S$ is proper, flat, finitely presented, of pure relative dimension one, with nodal geometrically reduced fibres. Each $H_u$ is a union of entire irreducible components of $Z_u$, with their reduced structures. Let $J\subset N$ be the reduced closure of $N\setminus H$ and let $B=H\times_N J$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection. Both $B\to S$ and $Q\times_N H\to S$ are finite etale, their supports are disjoint, and they lie in the relative smooth locus of $H$. For every geometric point $\bar u\to S$, the support of $B_{\bar u}$ is exactly $H_{\bar u}\cap\overline{N_{\bar u}\setminus H_{\bar u}}$. In particular the integer
$$|H_{\bar u}\cap\overline{N_{\bar u}\setminus H_{\bar u}}|+|Q_{\bar u}\cap H_{\bar u}|$$
is independent of $\bar u$ and equals its value on a geometric generic fibre. No genus-zero hypothesis, numerical bound on this integer, or morphism contracting $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Auxiliary relative-component closure claim for the details omitted in Temkin Lemma 4.4.4, referring to Lemma 4.4.2 (arXiv:0707.3953v3, pp. 30--32). The local models are Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), and the fibrewise complementary-subcurve boundary is Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve). Neither tag by itself states the relative closure claim; it is a separate statement to split.

proof.text: The closure of the nonempty irreducible space $|A|$ is irreducible by [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure]. By its reduced induced structure $H$ is reduced, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its closed immersion into the proper $S$-scheme $Z$ makes $H\to S$ proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The valuation ring $R$ is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal]; each localization is again a valuation ring (the valuation alternative persists) and hence normal as well.

source.place: Initial closure and properness; algebra.tex Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal), morphisms.tex Tag 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper).

proof.text: At each nonsmooth point of $N/S$, [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] gives etale charts $U\to N$, $V\to S$, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-a)$. Restrict to affine neighbourhoods. Since $S$ is normal integral with separably closed function field, [sbc-lem-etale-over-normal](1) applies to the separated etale affine map $V\to S$. Restricting to one of its open-immersion components identifies $V$ with an open of $S$. Every nonempty open of the finite chain $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is principal: if its complement is nonempty, choose an element in the least omitted prime and outside the largest retained prime; if the complement is empty use $1$. Thus $V=\operatorname{Spec}R_r$ after shrinking, a normal valuation domain. At smooth points [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] instead gives etale polynomial charts over an open of $S$. All resulting $U\to N$ form a jointly surjective etale family.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09Z9 (lemma-etale-over-normal); smooth etale polynomial charts Tag 054L.

proof.text: Closure and reduction commute with the etale source charts just chosen. Indeed, for any open map $e:U\to N$ and subset $T\subset N$, one has $e^{-1}\overline T=\overline{e^{-1}T}$: every open neighbourhood of a point on the left has open image meeting $T$, and thus meets $e^{-1}T$; the reverse inclusion is continuity. The charts are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Their pullbacks of reduced closed subschemes are reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. Uniqueness of reduced induced closed structures in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) therefore identifies $H_U$ with the reduced closure of $A\times_NU$, and $J_U$ with the reduced closure of $U\setminus H_U$. This argument requires no quasi-compactness of $N\setminus H$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY charts; topology of open maps, and schemes.tex Tags 01J3/01J4 (reduced induced structure).

proof.text: Write a chart as $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset S$ and put $F=\operatorname{Frac}D=L$. The closed generic subcurve $A_U$ is reduced: its map to $A$ is etale, so [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] applies. It is smooth of pure relative dimension one by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2). The generic ambient chart is a reduced pure curve: it is etale over a polynomial curve or over $F[u,v]/(uv-a)$, whose irreducible components are one-dimensional; etale local rings have the same Krull dimension by [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension]. The corresponding components have dimension one by the local-dimension criterion for locally algebraic schemes [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. These finite-type field schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Consequently [lem-trf-complementary-pure-subcurve-components] makes $A_U$ a reduced union of generic components. The ideal of its closure is the contraction of the intersection of the corresponding minimal primes: a section vanishes on the closure exactly when its generic restriction vanishes on those components, by the vanishing description of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](1). Apply [lem-trf-generic-subcurve-nodal-chart-ideals] to this subset.

source.place: Relative contraction of generic component ideals in Tag 0CBY charts; Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), component-union argument.

proof.text: On the smaller principal charts supplied by the ideal lemma, $H_U$ is empty, all of $U$, or one coordinate axis of a persistent model $uv=0$. The first two cases are flat and locally finitely presented over the base: they are empty or restrictions of the given flat locally finitely presented $N/S$. In the axis case $C/(u)$ is etale over $D[v]$, or $C/(v)$ over $D[u]$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. The affine line is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; composition with the etale axis map is smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2), hence flat and locally finitely presented by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]. Flatness descends from this surjective etale source cover by [lem-pc-flat-source-descent], and local finite presentation by [lem-trf-lfp-fppf-source-locality]. Finally properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness; together with local finite presentation this is finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 0CBY model; descent.tex Tag 036K (lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source) and Tag 036N (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-fppf-local-source).

proof.text: These local forms persist after every residue-field extension. The full chart contributes the given nodal geometrically reduced pure curve; an axis contributes a smooth reduced pure curve; empty charts contribute nothing. Pure dimension one and nodal completed local rings descend along the geometric etale chart cover by [lem-trf-etale-cover-field-curve-nodality], and reducedness is local on these faithfully flat charts (injection into the reduced local chart rings). Thus $H/S$ has the required fibres. The same forms show that each $H_u$ is a reduced closed union of whole components of $Z_u$: at full-chart points it equals the ambient fibre locally, and at an axis it is a whole branch, never an isolated point or a proper closed piece of a branch. Equivalently apply [lem-trf-complementary-pure-subcurve-components] to the reduced pure curves $Z_u,H_u$, which are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 0E38, reduced pure subcurves and their nodal fibres; Tag 0CBY chart calculation after residue-field extension.

proof.text: Compute $J_U$ from the open complement, using Step 3. Where the ideal of $H_U$ is $0$ or $1$, the complementary closure is respectively empty or all of $U$, so $B_U$ is empty. Where that ideal is $(u)$ in $C$ etale over $D[u,v]/(uv)$, the complementary reduced closure has ideal $(v)$: the basis $1,u^i,v^j$ of [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] shows $\operatorname{ann}(u^n)=(v)$ for every $n>0$ (multiplication shifts the $u$ coefficients and kills precisely the positive $v$ coefficients), which remains true after flat etale base change by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; hence $\ker(C\to C[1/u])=(v)$. Its quotient is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], since $C/(v)$ is etale over the reduced polynomial ring. The swapped case is identical. Thus $B_U=\operatorname{Spec}C/(u,v)$, etale over $\operatorname{Spec}D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. On $H_U$ this is the zero section in its smooth axis, so it lies in the relative smooth locus. Descent through the covering $B_U\to B$ using [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] makes $B/S$ etale; smoothness along its support descends by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness].

source.place: Tag 0CBY persistent model uv=0 and Tag 0E38 complementary-branch intersection; algebra.tex flat tensor exactness.

proof.text: The same calculation proves the asserted geometric-fibre equality, without asserting that every complementary closure commutes with base change. On a full or empty chart both boundaries are empty after any field extension. On an axis chart the complementary fibrewise closure is the other entire axis, and their intersection is $u=v=0$. Etale maps are open, so Step 3's neighbourhood argument applies also on geometric fibres. These equalities of supports can be checked on their surjective etale cover; they give $|B_{\bar u}|=|H_{\bar u}\cap\overline{N_{\bar u}\setminus H_{\bar u}}|$. Moreover, on the relative smooth locus of $N/S$ only the full and empty cases occur, by the smooth polynomial case of [lem-trf-generic-subcurve-nodal-chart-ideals]. Hence $H$ restricts there to an open-and-closed subscheme. It follows that $Q\times_NH$ is open and closed in $Q$, is etale over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1)--(2), and lies in the relative smooth locus of $H$. It is disjoint from $B$, whose nonempty charts lie at $u=v=0$, the nonsmooth points of $N/S$.

source.place: Tag 0E38 fibrewise complementary boundary; smooth polynomial charts from Tag 054L; Tag 0CBY node charts.

proof.text: Both $B$ and $Q\times_NH$ are closed subschemes of $H$: they are the pullbacks of the closed immersions $J\hookrightarrow N$ and $Q\hookrightarrow N$, respectively [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. They are therefore proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. An etale morphism is locally quasi-finite, by the zero-dimensional-fibre statement [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; the proper quasi-finite criterion [cor-pqf-proper-quasifinite-finite] now makes both finite. This criterion imposes no Noetherian hypothesis on $S$. Finally $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is connected: its generic point is dense, so any nonempty open contains it and there is no disconnection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree](a)--(b) separately to the two finite etale schemes. Their geometric point counts are constant, including degree zero. Adding these two constants and using Step 8's support identification proves precisely the displayed integer formula, including equality with the geometric generic value.

source.place: more-morphisms.tex Tag 02LS (lemma-characterize-finite); finite-etale geometric degree over a connected base.

proof_origin.place: Relative generic-subcurve closure calculation reconstructed from the local models of Tag 0CBY and the fibrewise subcurve argument of Tag 0E38. The additional local algebra lemma is stated separately; no global relative closure theorem is attributed to either tag.

The statement is unchanged and no DAG node duplicates it: lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary and lem-trf-stacks-nodal-closed-subcurve are only the fibrewise 0E38. Step 2: 09Z9(1) applies because V is affine étale over affine S, hence separated, and S is normal with separably closed function field. A nonempty open of the finite prime chain equals D(r) for r in p_k minus p_{k-1}. Step 3: closure commutes with pullback along open maps, and uniqueness of the reduced induced structure identifies H_U and J_U. Step 4: A_U is a reduced union of generic components with contracted ideal, so the new node applies over D=R_r. Step 5: flatness and finite presentation descend along the étale chart cover (036K, the fppf-source node), and proper plus lfp gives fp. Step 6: purity, nodality and reducedness transfer through the chart cover by lem-trf-etale-cover-field-curve-nodality and faithful flatness. Step 7: ann_E(u^n)=(v) in D[u,v]/(uv) by the binomial basis, kept after flat tensoring, so the boundary is C/(u,v), étale over D, and étaleness descends through the source cover. Step 8: the geometric supports agree by the same computation over Ω, H is clopen on the smooth locus so Q×H is clopen in Q, and B sits at nonsmooth points. Step 9: cor-pqf with no base hypothesis gives finiteness, and the finite-étale degree lemma over the connected Spec R gives the constant count.
